Treatment summary
Patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which the patient's vehicle was struck while turning left.
Complaints centered on neck and low back pain with associated muscle guarding and reduced range of motion in the
cervical and lumbar spine. The mechanism of injury described is consistent with the symptoms reported. Some
objective findings on examination, including palpable paraspinal tenderness and restricted motion, support the clinical
diagnosis of cervical and lumbar strain. Other neurological and orthopedic tests performed during the evaluation were
wihtin normal limits. No prior injury or treatment to the neck or back is known. The patient completed 25 visits of
conservative care, including manual therapy, stretching, and home exercise instruction. Progress has been gradual,
and the course of treatment ran somewhat longer than is typical for this type of strain. Billing records reviewed for this
episode of care show no duplicated or repeated charges. Ongoing management includes continued home exercise
and reassessment at the next scheduled follow-up.
